humanities_role_explanation: SimpleQA is a general short-form factuality benchmark. History (n=173), Art (n=550) and Music (n=341) questions are just topic tags among science, politics, sports, TV and video games. The items test generic fact retrieval and calibration, not disciplinary competence in any humanities field.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only questions and short text answers.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Short, fact-seeking questions with a single indisputable answer (dates, persons, numbers, places), graded correct/incorrect/not attempted. The paper also measures calibration via stated confidence and answer frequency ("know what they know"). There is no interpretive work.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad-topic factuality benchmark spanning science, politics, art, geography, sports, music, TV, history and more. It is scoped to the single task of short-form factual QA.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Claude-3 haiku/sonnet/opus, Claude-3.5-sonnet, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, o1-mini, o1-preview.

quantitative_metrics.note: Correct, not attempted, incorrect, correct given attempted, F-score, calibration plots.

summary: SimpleQA is a 4,326-question benchmark of short, fact-seeking questions with single, indisputable answers. It was adversarially collected against GPT-4 responses. It evaluates factual accuracy, abstention behaviour and calibration of frontier models.
key_findings: Frontier models score low: o1-preview reaches 42.7% correct and GPT-4o 38.2%. Claude models abstain far more often than GPT-4o, so their F-scores are similar. Larger models are better calibrated, but all overstate their confidence. The authors estimate a benchmark error rate of about 3%.
facets_explanation: Question and answer pairs were written by AI trainers (human annotators) who supplied a supporting web source. A second trainer answered independently and only matching items were kept. Questions with several valid answers or conflicting sources were removed, and the paper reports ambiguous or multi-answer items as errors. The annotators are not described as disciplinary experts, and the paper does not say whether the trainers belonged to the authors' organisation, so 'paper_authors' is the closest label, not a confident one. The questions require outside knowledge, since the model sees only the question.
results_explanation: Table 3 lists OpenAI o1-preview with Correct 42.7, Correct given attempted 47.0 and F-score 44.8, and GPT-4o with Correct 38.2. The best score is the overall 'Correct' percentage, treated here as accuracy. A third trainer scored 94.4% on 1,000 sampled items, but this checks dataset quality and is not a human baseline against which models are compared. No format comparison or cultural comparison is reported.

humanities_role.quote: SimpleQA contains questions from a wide range of topics, including history, science & technology, art, geography, TV shows, etc.

dataset_size.quote: We present a benchmark called SimpleQA, which contains 4,326 short, fact-seeking questions.

gold_source.quote: First, AI trainers (i.e., human annotators) created question and answer pairs.

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: we asked AI trainers to create knowledge-seeking questions that fit a very specific set of criteria.

answer_multiplicity.quote: questions were written in such a way that the predicted answers are easily gradable.
